sourceInformation.genre: Surgical action game with hospital drama and ward exploration
sourceInformation.perspective: First-person top-down surgery; portrait story stages; three-quarter ward and cinematics; side-view title
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge 0.89.1, AI Hub client 1.4.0, JavaScript, Canvas 2D and Web Audio. Engine patches: touch notice, adaptive sizing and mouse input switching.
sourceInformation.artDirection: PS1-style pixel art, wet tissue with palette ramps and ordered dithering, polygon portraits and procedural surgical instruments. Kenney CC0 furniture.
sourceInformation.animation: Native Humanoid rigs with custom scrub, operate, pass, push and knitting poses; procedural organs, parasites, instruments and story portraits.
sourceInformation.audio: Synthesized music, surgical effects, formant-based gibberish voices and parasite choir. Music defaults to 10%.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, shared world, 1–4 players; local co-op and AI colleagues.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless tools and a scripted whole-campaign playthrough; screenshots for visual checks. Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, emulated controllers, 14 viewports and all Hub scenarios. WebKit is the iOS stand-in. One quiet test command; no subagents.
sourceInformation.research: Read PLAN.md and the current engine README, API, asset guide and Hub protocol; inspected the native adventure kit and furniture catalogue. No additional source-game research.

testingFeedback: 16 issues found during automated tests and visual checks; 7 additional defects fixed during implementation checks. All 23 fixes are logged.
2 critical defects, fixed: mixed keyboard/mouse control and missing remote Code Blue state. No known game-breaking issues remain.
The full campaign scene playthrough verified story progression, all operations, ward transitions, ending, credits, saves and ranks. Live Hub strokes isolated the mixed-input defect.
The generic key-mashing engine check stayed in the first tutorial; its scripted inputs added little beyond its useful drawing and visual checks.
engineFeedback: The deterministic fixed-step headless runtime, native pixel primitives and continuous Humanoid rigs made simulation tests and original procedural art practical.
Yes. Projected joints include depth; spreading them into a 2D line distorted hats. Story.skip affects newly opened lines. Pointer movement originally kept keyboard as the last input device.
The JSON-safe surgical simulation: eight tool gestures, tissue painter integration, strain state machines, exact rewind, checkpoints, bot input and host-authoritative networking.
Coordinating field, screen and CSS coordinates while keeping mouse, pad, bot and remote gestures consistent.

Moved the touch-only notice to the bottom with a working Settings button; allowed fixed-resolution downscaling in small frames and fractional high-DPR fitting; restored mouse input on pointer movement after keyboard use.
Separate pointer aim ownership from prompt-device tracking explicitly, with a documented mixed keyboard/mouse pattern.
promptFeedback: The concrete game plan, original cast, verified engine recipes and explicit offline packaging and test requirements gave the work a clear direction.
The exhaustive scope and optional cuts pull in different directions. The full plan was used as the target. The named testing-toolkit cheatsheet was absent, so the supplied instructions were used.
Making precise surgical gestures behave consistently for mouse, controller, imperfect bots and lossy multiplayer while completing the campaign and presentation.
Add machine-readable acceptance cases and fixture inputs for continuous gestures alongside the narrative plan.

aiHub.name: Trauma Sector: Second Signal
aiHub.description: A rookie surgeon and a deadpan nurse race to save patients from a parasite that sings. Eleven cases, eight tools and two impossible gifts; work alone or share the table with up to four surgeons.
aiHub.controls: Aim: right stick or mouse. Use: R2 or click. Tools: left stick or 1-8. Gift: Triangle or F.
